paper.title: Melting, Processing, and Properties of Disordered Fe-Al and Fe-Al-C Based Alloys
paper.paper_scope: Investigation of melting routes (AIM, AIMFC, VIM), thermomechanical processing, and mechanical properties of disordered Fe-7 wt.% Al and Fe-9 wt.% Al lightweight steels, and the effect of carbon (0.02-1.0 wt.%) on the microstructure and properties of Fe-7Al alloys.

alloys.description: Disordered Fe-Al solid solution alloy with nominal 7 wt.% Al, chosen as a totally disordered solid solution; base lightweight steel studied across AIM, AIMFC, and VIM melting routes.
alloys.alloys_notes: Measured composition (Table I) depends on melting process: Al 7.02-7.30, Si 0.12-0.20, Mn 0.045-0.056, S 0.0016-0.0075, C 0.015-0.021, O 0.0035-0.0200 wt.%. Low-carbon (~0.02 wt.% C) base alloy.

source.reason: Fe-7 wt.% Al disordered solid solution alloy is the primary aluminum level selected for the melting/processing study.

alloys.description: Fe-Al alloy with nominal 9 wt.% Al, expected to exhibit short-range ordering; second aluminum level studied alongside Fe-7Al.
alloys.alloys_notes: Measured composition (Table I): Al 9.10-9.20, Si 0.11-0.16, Mn 0.042-0.046, S 0.0015-0.0027, C 0.014-0.017 wt.% for AIMFC and VIM. The AIM ingot of Fe-9Al exhibited extensive gas porosity and was not analyzed.

source.reason: Fe-9 wt.% Al alloy is the second aluminum level selected for the study (expected to exhibit short-range ordering).

alloys.description: Carbon-free reference Fe-7Al alloy in the carbon-effect study (Table IV, serial no. 1).
alloys.alloys_notes: Table IV reports C 0.002 wt.% (Al 6.86, Si 0.18, Mn 0.16, S 0.004); the text (b0059) states the carbon range as 0.02-1.0 wt.% and Fig. 5 labels the baseline 0.012 wt.% C, indicating inconsistent reporting of the baseline carbon level.

source.reason: Carbon-free baseline alloy explicitly listed in Table IV of the carbon-effect study.

processes.process_name: Air induction melting + hot forging + hot rolling
processes.description: Air induction melting (AIM) of Fe-7Al; ingot preheated at 1373 K for 1 h, hot forged, then hot rolled by 50% to 12 mm thickness.
processes.processes_notes: Fe-9Al produced by AIM exhibited extensive gas porosity and could not be thermomechanically processed; this process therefore yields a characterized sample only for Fe-7Al.

source.reason: AIM is one of the three melting routes studied; the resulting sound Fe-7Al ingot was hot-forged and hot-rolled for property evaluation.

processes.process_name: Air induction melting with flux cover + hot forging + hot rolling
aliases: air induction melting with flux cover
processes.description: Air induction melting with a protective flux cover (Al2O3, CaO, MgO, CaF2) and proprietary charging schedule; melt held at 1900 K for 2 min; ingot preheated at 1373 K/1 h, hot forged, and hot rolled 50% to 12 mm.
processes.processes_notes: Applied to Fe-7Al, Fe-9Al, and the Fe-7Al-C carbon-series alloys. Note: Table V and Fig. 5 captions for the carbon-series label the route 'AIM', while the section text (b0060) states the alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover.

source.reason: AIMFC is the newly developed cost-effective melting route; sound ingots were subsequently hot-forged and hot-rolled.

processes.process_name: Vacuum induction melting + hot forging + hot rolling
processes.description: Vacuum induction melting (50-kg, 125-kW, 10^-4 torr); melt poured at 1893 K into 80-mm split cast iron molds; ingot preheated at 1373 K/1 h, hot forged, and hot rolled 50% to 12 mm.
processes.processes_notes: Applied to both Fe-7Al and Fe-9Al; used for comparison with AIM and AIMFC.

source.reason: VIM is the comparison melting route; sound ingots were hot-forged and hot-rolled for property evaluation.

processes.process_name: AIMFC + hot working + cold rolling + annealing
processes.description: AIMFC Fe-7Al ingot hot-forged and hot-rolled, then cold-rolled to thin sheets (2 mm) and foils, followed by annealing; exhibited excellent room-temperature ductility (~40% total elongation).
processes.processes_notes: Table III reports room-temperature tensile properties of the 2-mm cold-rolled and annealed sheet.

source.reason: Cold-rolled and annealed condition of AIMFC Fe-7Al is a distinct end state characterized in Table III.

processes.description: VIM Fe-7Al ingot hot-forged and hot-rolled, then cold-rolled to thin sheets and foils.
processes.processes_notes: Mentioned as cold-rollable to thin sheets and foils (b0041); no separate tensile data are reported for this cold-rolled VIM condition.

source.reason: Cold-rolling of VIM Fe-7Al to sheets and foils is reported as a distinct processing path.

unmapped_findings: Background (not studied objects): ordered Fe-Al-C alloys containing 11 and 16 wt.% Al, and Fe-16Al-1C / Fe-11Al-1C, are prior DMRL work described in the introduction (b0007).
The carbon-series samples are described in b0060 as prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (AIMFC), but Table V and Fig. 5 captions label them 'AIM'; this inconsistency is noted.
Fe-9Al produced by AIM exhibited extensive gas porosity and was not analyzed nor thermomechanically processed (b0015, b0041, b0049).
